summary: The brand mark and the login screen are now standardized across every app. The shield/eye/checkmark mark moved into the shared UI module as @shared/BrandLogo (with a matching brand.css), so the three hand-copied SVGs can no longer drift; each app supplies only its wordmark and a --brand-mark hue token, deliberately set outside the theme blocks so the brand keeps its identity in light and dark. The geometry and saturation are identical and only the hue moves - mymatasan green, myseliasan steel, myidsan violet - so the apps read as one family while staying tellable apart in a browser tab strip. The password input with its in-field reveal toggle moved to @shared/PasswordField on the same basis. MySeliaSan gained a real favicon (its previous .ico was an unrelated image) and its login, forced-password-change and pending-clearance screens now wear mymatasan's login-panel chrome. MyIDSan had no favicon and no asset pipeline at all; it now has both, and its server-rendered federated sign-in page - the page MySeliaSan hands the browser to during SSO - wears the same card, so the whole federated flow looks like one product. A failed login on that page now re-renders the branded card with the error inline and the username preserved, instead of dumping unstyled text.
compatibility: Purely presentational; no schema, config or API changes. Fixes a live bug in MySeliaSan: its login card was styled background: var(--bg-panel, #fff) and --bg-panel was never defined anywhere, so the card stayed white in dark and high-contrast themes while the page behind it went near-black.
